ashfield|secondary_street_setback|dwelli.note: VERDICT CHANGED from the first pass, which accepted it narrowly with an applicability qualifier. The clause is real and correctly read -- buildings on the Parramatta Road Enterprise Corridor that adjoin a heritage conservation area are set back 3m from the secondary street -- and it comes from chapter-d-precinct-guidelines, gated further on adjoining an HCA. The deciding fact, checked this time and not last time: NOTHING FILTERS ON applicability. The single guarded read -- scripts/conveyancing_db.py fetch_dcp_setbacks, which every surface proxies -- filters on lga, is_current and needs_review only. A row marked precinct_specific is therefore served to every property in the LGA, told apart from a general control by nothing but its condition text. There are already 7 such rows live, including a leichhardt 1.0m front setback taken from Birchgrove and Balmain neighbourhood minimums. Marking scope in a column that no consumer reads does not contain the scope. Ashfield already carries one precinct row served this way (Haberfield Yasmar Estate, front_setback 4.0m). Ashfield therefore ends with no secondary street setback, which is the honest state: it has no general one in the extracted text.

hornsby|secondary_street_setback|dwellin.note: NEW and clean. Table 3.1.2-a's own heading on the page is 'Minimum boundary setbacks for dwellings and dual occupancies', and the row reads 'Secondary boundary 3m (on corner lots)'. LGA-wide, boundary-relative, ground level, mandatory table. Corroborated by our own data: hornsby already serves front, rear and side setbacks extracted from the same table (section_ref 's3.1.2-table-a'), so this completes that set with the one boundary that was missing. dev_type dwelling_house; the table also governs dual occupancies, which the next row states in its own terms.

hornsby|secondary_street_setback|dual_oc.note: NEW. Prescriptive measure (h) on the same page reads 'An attached dual occupancy on a corner lot should have both dwellings address the primary road frontage', so the clause's subject is dual occupancy, and (i) gives it 3m to the secondary road. Same value as the dwelling-house row above, from a different clause about a different dev_type -- so not a duplicate: a consumer querying dual_occupancy would otherwise get nothing.

hornsby|secondary_street_setback|residen.note: NEW, and the qualifier is the control. dev_type comes from our own extracted provisions, which give the part title as '3.4 Residential Flat Buildings (5 Storeys)'; 3.4.5 is its setbacks sub-section. The 6m applies only 'Where a secondary frontage adjoins an existing laneway (with no verge)'. That is a site condition, not a geography, so unlike the Pound Road rows below it is genuinely LGA-wide -- but served without its test it would read as hornsby's general apartment secondary setback, which it is not. Qualifier moved to the front of the condition.

corrections.condition: ONLY WHERE a secondary frontage adjoins an EXISTING LANEWAY with no verge: all buildings and structures should be set back a minimum of 6 metres from that boundary. This is not hornsby's general secondary street setback for residential flat buildings.

marrickville|secondary_street_setback|mu.note: VERDICT CHANGED from the first pass, which corrected 4.5 to 6 and accepted it. Checking our own table settles it the other way: marrickville ALREADY holds multi_dwelling_housing front_setback 6.0m at section_ref 's4.2.4.3-C11(i)' -- this same clause, this same 6m, correctly read as the FRONT setback. Limb (a) says 'Must be 6 metres from the front boundary'; limb (b) says the secondary building line 'may, at the discretion of Council, be reduced to 4.5 metres'. So the clause states a concession without ever stating the secondary requirement it reduces from. 4.5 asserts an entitlement nobody has; 6 re-serves the primary figure as the secondary one, which is precisely the defect DQ-40 created secondary_street_setback to fix ('20 rows served a 2-4m secondary setback as the 4.5-6m primary'). Neither number can be stored, so neither is.

marrickville|secondary_street_setback|mi.note: GRAIN, and the datum is what decides it. The clause requires upper levels to be set back 6 metres 'from the street front of the building' -- measured from the building's own street frontage, not from a property boundary. Every other row in this column is boundary-relative, so storing it here puts a building-relative number in a boundary-relative field, where nothing marks the difference. Compounded by the second half of the grain problem: it governs upper levels above the street front portion only, not the setback at ground level that this control type answers.
